title: [state engine] Runtime-VAL manifest normalization fails on Python 3.14 member descriptors
description: Confirmed on assessment baseline af79b34040f5ce5fd989aa0d42a1b80ad8366829. A clean detached worktree ran plain `uv sync --frozen --all-extras`; because pyproject.toml declares `requires-python = ">=3.12"`, uv selected CPython 3.14.3. EV-002 (`tests/integration/pipeline/test_builtin_sink_effect_recovery.py` plus `tests/unit/core/landscape/test_scheduler_repository_complete_barrier.py`) then produced 9 failures and 30 passes. All 9 fail while building the Runtime-VAL manifest: `_normalize_dependency_value` raises FrameworkBugError for `elspeth.contracts.errors:__classdict__[value]` of type `builtins:member_descriptor` (representative candidate: `PassThroughContractViolation.divergence_set`). Recreating the same worktree-local environment with `uv sync --python 3.13 --frozen --all-extras` on CPython 3.13.1 makes the same vector pass 39/39; the other carried-forward vectors pass 46/46, 30/30, and 13/13. Exit gate: add deterministic Python 3.14 member_descriptor normalization that preserves Runtime-VAL semantic hashing, with focused 3.13/3.14 compatibility tests and the affected state-engine vector green on both. Do not narrow the advertised Python range merely to hide the defect without a separate support decision.
